component.name: ink-notes
component.summary: Handwritten notes with pen, touch and mouse
Notizbuch-App für Stift, Touch und Maus

description.p: ink-notes is a notebook app for Linux tablets and convertibles. Handwriting is stored as vectors; write with a pen, your finger, a touchpad or a mouse.
ink-notes ist eine Notizbuch-App für Linux-Tablets und Convertibles. Handschrift wird als Vektoren gespeichert; geschrieben wird mit Stift, Finger, Touchpad oder Maus.
Features:
Funktionen:

ul.li: Pens and highlighter with pressure, smoothing while writing and sharp corners
Stifte und Textmarker mit Druckstärke, Glättung beim Schreiben und Ecken-Erhaltung
Shape recognition: hold at the end of a stroke to get clean lines, arrows, circles, rectangles, triangles and coordinate systems
Formerkennung: am Strichende halten für saubere Linien, Pfeile, Kreise, Rechtecke, Dreiecke und Koordinatensysteme
Eraser for whole strokes, partial strokes or highlighter only; virtual ruler
Radierer für ganze Striche, Teilstriche oder nur Textmarker; virtuelles Lineal
Select, move, rotate, scale and recolor; undo for every change
Auswählen, Verschieben, Drehen, Skalieren und Umfärben; Rückgängig für alle Änderungen
Text boxes, images and PDF import to annotate lecture slides and worksheets
Textfelder, Bilder und PDF-Import zum Beschriften von Vorlesungsfolien und Übungsblättern
Notebooks in folders, continuous scrolling, automatic saving in the background
Notizbücher in Ordnern, durchgehendes Scrollen, automatisches Speichern im Hintergrund
Export as PDF (with searchable text), PNG or SVG
Export als PDF (mit durchsuchbarem Text), PNG oder SVG

description.p: Windows: the mouse works again; Windows Ink no longer reports it as a pen.
First experimental Windows version as a portable program. Internal groundwork for Android; nothing changes on Linux.

The notebooks can be stored in a folder synced by Nextcloud, Google Drive, Syncthing or Dropbox. Changes from other devices are taken over automatically, conflict copies become pages of their own, and a warning appears when a notebook is open on another device.
Saber notebooks (.sbn2, .sba, .sbn) can be imported as new notebooks, with strokes, pen pressure, highlighters, shapes, typed text, images and PDF backgrounds.
Notebooks from Xournal++ (.xopp, .xoj) and Rnote (.rnote) can be imported as new notebooks, with strokes, pen pressure, highlighters, shapes, texts, images and backgrounds.
PDF and PNG export and copying a selection as an image are about six times faster, and exported PDFs are much smaller, because stroke outlines are simplified invisibly before export.
The swipe speed for gliding is measured with the touch screen's own event times, so a swipe still glides when the app handles the lift a little late.
A finger swipe is measured reliably again for gliding, also when the view touches the edge of the notebook. The fling diagnostics log more details.
The eraser size is set in a menu like the pens, with presets and a slider. Corners of snapped shapes stay pointed. Slides get flat tiles in the page overview.

The hand is ignored while the pen is near the screen, also on the title bar. The eraser comes in four sizes. The page overview shows imported PDF pages. Snapped triangles and other shapes have the same width on every side. A selection made with the pen's select button can be moved with the pen.

The endless canvas starts at the top left and grows to the right and down. New text fields start short and grow with the text. The toolbar buttons are larger again on small screens. On Wayland, the title bar buttons work with a finger.
New view-only mode: with 👁 in the toolbar, pen, finger and mouse only scroll and zoom, and nothing can be changed by accident.
Ctrl+Plus and Ctrl+Minus zoom only the page again, no longer the whole interface. Text boxes being edited now sit exactly where the text ends up.

Snapped highlighter shapes keep the highlighter width. Sharp corners such as the tip of a "1" are drawn round instead of cut off, and strokes no longer jump when the pen lifts. Finger swipes glide more reliably.

Faster scrolling through long notebooks and PDFs: a quick finger swipe keeps gliding, and a scrollbar with page numbers jumps through the notebook. The mouse wheel scrolls further per step. New notebooks scroll continuously by default.
Moving, rotating and scaling large selections is smooth again and no longer keeps the processor busy. On endless notebooks the mouse wheel scrolls (Ctrl+wheel zooms).

Endless notebooks: one surface without edges to write, pan and zoom in every direction. Choose it when creating a notebook or switch a single-page notebook in the menu; PDF export contains only the written area.
Each notebook remembers whether it flips page by page or scrolls continuously. New notebooks start with fixed pages; the layout can be chosen when creating a notebook and changed later in the menu.
The pens in the toolbar are shown as pencils in their own colour, so they are easy to tell apart.
Pictures keep their proportions when resized. A lock button in the selection tool switches between proportional and free resizing; pictures start locked, other objects free.
Smoother scrolling through large imported PDFs: pages no longer stall the display while they are prepared, and pages scrolled past quickly are skipped.
Screenshots in the app description for software centers. The app itself is unchanged.
Select and move objects with a finger; text and make-space tools also work with a finger. Exports go to the documents folder of the user directories.
English user interface; the language follows the system and can be changed in the menu. Holding to snap a shape tolerates a slightly trembling pen.
Axis cross from two crossing strokes.
The on-screen keyboard of GNOME appears when tapping a text field.
